criteria.note: The keyword intent ("is tteok gluten-free?") is resolved in the opening block — glutinous rice has no gluten, but 밀떡 is wheat, so the category cannot be cleared — well inside the first 200 words.

Title with the rendered suffix is ~58 chars, description ~146 chars, keyword present in the title as "Gluten-Free Tteok", and the description advances new information (밀떡, cost) rather than restating the title.
Headings carry the argument rather than label it — a skimmer gets glutinous≠gluten → but 밀떡 is wheat → dessert is the gap → the price → make it yourself → where to buy the flours.
Five in-body links across four destinations (hidden-gluten guide, Monil2 House, celiac travel guide), each placed where the reader would actually want the detour.
All three FAQ answers are established in the body — the GIG citation, the 밀떡/소맥분 label check, and the shared-equipment/reformulation caveats — and each reads standalone as a rich result.
Concrete but thin: one real receipt figure and a home batch, but no shop, no date of purchase, no quantities for the bake, and nothing that went wrong in the kitchen.
criteria.evidence_quote: I'm not going to hand you exact gram-by-gram ratios, because I worked mostly by feel and I'd rather not invent precision I didn't measure.

criteria.note: Korean terms are consistently romanised and the regulation is cited to a numbered 고시, but the piece names no product, brand, or seller anywhere — including in the section titled "Sourcing the two flours" — and its cost thesis is quantified on only one side.
criteria.evidence_quote: So I did. I ordered **glutinous rice flour and tapioca starch**, picked up a **mold**, and gave it a go.

criteria.note: Primary sources are linked and dated: the MFDS notice is cited as 고시 제2025-60호, 29 August 2025 alongside the 식품등의 표시기준 text, and the GIG FAQ carries a retrieval date.

The piece states repeatedly what it cannot establish — the anecdote disclaimer, the withdrawn No Brand claim, the "operator's claim" caveat on the dedicated bakery — and carries no commercial links to disclose.

findings.quote: What you can reliably find is the two flours sold separately, and sellers who bundle them as a pair.
findings.why: The section promising sourcing names no product, brand, retailer, or price for either flour, so the reader leaves with an instruction they cannot act on — and this is the one section where a searcher on a buying intent lands.
findings.fix: Name at least one verified product for each flour (brand + 제품명 + pack size) and where it was bought, with the date checked; if nothing could be verified, say so explicitly the way the No Brand withdrawal does.

findings.quote: cheaper by the batch than by the piece
findings.why: The article's central turn is a cost argument but only the cafe side is quantified (6,000 won / 3 pieces + 500 won); with no ingredient cost or yield, the payoff claim is unverifiable by the reader.
findings.fix: Add the purchase price of each flour bag, the approximate yield of one home batch, and a per-piece figure so the comparison is checkable.

findings.quote: Around **6,000 won for three pieces, plus another 500 won to add condensed milk.**
findings.why: The strongest first-hand detail has no shop, neighbourhood, or date attached, so it reads as a remembered figure rather than an observed one and cannot be corroborated.
findings.fix: Anchor the receipt to a place and month (e.g. "a cafe in Yeonnam, July 2026"), and add one specific thing that went wrong or surprised you in the first home batch.

findings.quote: <!-- IMG: 01.webp — homemade butter tteok, first batch, top-down on a plate. Caption: "Our first home batch — not bad at all." -->
findings.why: The only visual proof of the first-hand bake ships as an HTML comment, so it renders as nothing — the page loses both the scannability break and the strongest experience signal it has.
findings.fix: Publish the image with the caption and alt text, or delete the placeholder so the section does not depend on a picture readers never see.

findings.quote: So "tteok is rice, therefore tteok is gluten-free" is the wrong rule.
findings.why: The keyword is the broad "gluten free tteok", but after this correction the piece narrows entirely to butter tteok; common searches (떡국떡, 백설기, 인절미, packaged tteokbokki tteok) get no verdict, leaving the query only partly served.
findings.fix: Add a short scan-list of the common tteok types with a one-line rice/wheat verdict for each, then hand off to the butter tteok story as the worked example.

criteria.note: Sourced or self-marked throughout (GIG link, 고시 citation, 'I worked mostly by feel'), but the central four-ingredient composition is asserted with no source or observation marker; it is caveated enough that it does not by itself drive a safety decision.

criteria.note: Product names, prices, the 고시 number and date, and the frontmatter date (29 July 2026 is indeed a Wednesday) are internally consistent and checkable, and an unverifiable No Brand claim was withdrawn rather than retained.

The piece says where each load-bearing fact came from, gives retrieval dates, declines to invent measurement precision it did not take, and states plainly what reading a recipe or a label cannot establish.

No absolute clearance is given, cross-contamination is addressed at shop, kitchen, and flour-milling level, celiac risk is explicitly separated from NCGS, and the no-symptoms-is-not-proof point is stated outright.
Both external sources carry retrieval dates, the 고시 version is identified by number and date, and reformulation staleness is flagged as a standing limit rather than left implicit.
밀떡/쌀떡, 찹쌀가루, 소맥분, 원재료명, and 같은 제조시설 are used correctly, and the load-bearing fact — that the duty covers designated allergens with 밀 included but 보리 and 호밀 not — is stated accurately.
The reader is given concrete self-checks (scan 원재료명 for 밀/소맥분, look for the 같은 제조시설 line, ask the shop about recipe and kitchen) plus direct links to both primary sources and a correction address.

findings.why: The four-ingredient composition is the article's central permissive claim, and it is presented with no attribution — not to a specific product label, a named shop, or a published recipe. The surrounding caveats stop it from being actionable on its own, but a reader cannot check where the list came from.
findings.fix: Add one clause naming the provenance, e.g. 'the ingredient list on the bag we bought from [shop], August 2026' or 'the recipe as it is commonly published in Korean food blogs', so the reader knows whether this is a label reading or a genre description.

findings.quote: Most places selling butter tteok also bake wheat pastries, on the same counters and trays.
findings.why: A prevalence claim about Korean cafes stated as fact with no source or observation marker. It points in the safe direction, so it cannot cause harm, but it is unverifiable as written.
findings.fix: Mark it as observation — 'every cafe we have bought it from also baked wheat pastries' — or soften to 'assume the kitchen also handles wheat unless the shop tells you otherwise'.
